A technical SEO audit tied to decisions

A useful audit connects a technical observation to a specific URL, a proposed fix and a way to verify it. SiteSutra reviews the agreed public website and the search accounts you authorise, then separates confirmed problems from questions that need more evidence.

What an audit finding looks like

Hypothetical audit findings — examples of the handover format
ObservationRecommended actionAcceptance evidence
An old service URL returns an error after a redesign.Check whether an equivalent page exists and agree the appropriate redirect.The old URL reaches the agreed destination without a redirect chain.
Two service pages have the same title but answer different buyer questions.Write descriptive titles for the distinct page purposes.The rendered titles match approved content and remain unique.
A booking-link click is reported as a received enquiry.Separate click activity from confirmed bookings and qualified conversations.The report names each measure and its actual source.

Which access is needed?

A public crawl can start without account credentials. Search Console, Bing and analytics evidence require the account owner's approved access. Implementation also needs the relevant repository or platform access. Keep credentials in the provider's access controls, not a shared project brief.

Audit first, then agree implementation

The handover records affected URLs, evidence, business impact, owner and how to retest. Fixes can be scoped separately from content, campaigns or a redesign. For a wider change, use the redesign migration checklist; local businesses can review the Varanasi digital marketing overview.

Who this is for

Businesses and agencies with a website that needs a technical review, clearer service content or an agreed search-marketing plan. We prioritise fixes that support a real buyer journey.

Audit and implementation deliverables

Agree crawl and indexability checks, URL inventory, descriptive metadata, headings, internal links, canonical and sitemap review, redirect recommendations, structured-data review and a prioritised implementation plan. Campaign or content work is specified separately.

What is excluded

Guaranteed rankings, indexing, traffic, leads or AI recommendations are not deliverables. Paid media spend, large content programmes, link acquisition and third-party tools are separate; no purchased demand data is implied.

Process

Confirm business goals and access → establish a documented baseline → review pages and technical evidence → prioritise work → implement approved changes → validate and report limitations.

Commercial approach

Request a tailored quote for an audit, implementation project or ongoing review. Define URLs, access and reporting cadence before work starts; advertising spend is separate.

Relevant evidence

These buyer guides and SiteSutra’s crawlable service pages demonstrate content structure and technical foundations. The sample redirect map is hypothetical, not a client audit. No commercial performance results are claimed.

Three measures, three questions

Search visibility: impressions, clicks, queries and page coverage in verified search tools. AI citations: record dated prompts, assistant, cited URL and whether a citation actually appeared; this sample is not a market-wide visibility score. Qualified enquiries: record the source, service fit, goal, budget discussion and agreed next step after a real email or booking arrives. A booking-link click is not a confirmed enquiry.
